title: Tibet mega-dam (Motuo) value chain
map_limitation: Chinese SOE procurement is opaque: supplier awards surface late and partially. A-share beneficiaries re-rated on announcement day (limit-ups, July 2025), so local crowdedness is already elevated; the mapping question is which links remain unpriced OUTSIDE China. Links are unscored by design — run heat to score them with fetched evidence.

links.name: Power offtake & load centers
links.role: Where ~300 TWh/yr lands from the early 2030s [Reuters/CNBC, as of 2025-07]: eastern load centers via long-haul transmission plus Tibet-local industry; the demand anchor that justifies everything upstream.

bottleneck.note: Offtake is policy-assured; the constraint is delivery infrastructure, not demand.

impact.rationale: Policy-assured demand anchor, but value is diffuse across grid and end users; no single offtake P&L moves on it.

evidence.claim: ~300 TWh/yr planned output from early 2030s, absorbed into eastern load centers by policy design

crowdedness.rationale: Nobody trades 'offtake' as a security; zero retail or institutional narrative attaches here.

evidence.claim: Coverage focuses on builders and equipment names, never offtake economics

capture.rationale: Regulated transmission and planned-economy power pricing cap any capture.

evidence.claim: Chinese grid power tariffs are administratively set

links.name: China Yajiang Group (project owner)
links.role: New state-owned entity created to lead the 1.2 trillion yuan ($167B) five-cascade development [Bloomberg/Reuters, as of 2025-07]; the order book every supplier link sells into.

bottleneck.note: Single buyer; procurement pace sets the entire chain's revenue timing.

impact.rationale: The 1.2T yuan program IS the occurrence; its procurement pace times every supplier's revenue.

evidence.claim: China Yajiang Group created as dedicated SOE owner of the $167B five-cascade program

crowdedness.rationale: The headline entity of a front-page project; maximum narrative, no ticker to crowd into.

evidence.claim: Global front-page coverage of groundbreaking with Premier Li presiding

capture.rationale: SOE program vehicle; return maximization is not the objective function.

evidence.claim: State-directed infrastructure entity, unlisted

links.name: Civil construction & EPC
links.role: Five cascade stations in a Himalayan gorge, >40M cubic meters of concrete [CNBC, as of 2025-07]; PowerChina and China Energy Engineering rose limit-up on announcement.

bottleneck.note: SOE EPC capacity is deep; margins bid-competed — the volume-without-capture trap likely applies (score it).

impact.rationale: Five cascades and >40M m3 of concrete over a decade lands directly in SOE EPC orderbooks.

evidence.claim: PowerChina and China Energy Engineering rose by the 10% daily limit on announcement

crowdedness.rationale: Domestically crowded on announcement day (limit-ups), but blended attention has cooled; Western ownership minimal.

evidence.claim: A-share infrastructure names surged then mean-reverted as one-day narrative

capture.rationale: THE TRAP: bid-competed SOE EPC margins — enormous volume, thin capture; same structure as the AI chain's grid link.

evidence.claim: Chinese SOE EPC gross margins are structurally single-digit on mega-projects

links.name: Tunneling & TBMs
links.role: The design diverts the river's great bend through headrace tunnels; hard-rock TBMs and drill-blast at extreme altitude are the schedule-critical works.

bottleneck.note: Few suppliers of large hard-rock TBMs (CRCHI, China Railway Engineering Equipment; Herrenknecht private); geology risk concentrates here.

impact.rationale: Headrace tunnels through the Namcha Barwa massif are the schedule-critical, geology-risk works; TBM and drill-blast demand is front-loaded.

evidence.claim: Design diverts the great bend through tunnels; tunneling is the signature engineering challenge cited across project coverage

crowdedness.rationale: TBM makers barely feature in beneficiary lists; CRCHI is followed by domestic specialists only.

evidence.claim: Beneficiary coverage names cement and turbines, rarely tunneling equipment

capture.rationale: Few qualified large hard-rock TBM suppliers, but the customer is a monopsony SOE; pricing power partial.

evidence.claim: Large-diameter hard-rock TBM supply concentrated in CRCHI/CREG plus Herrenknecht (private)

links.name: Cement & materials at altitude
links.role: >16 million tons of cement implied [CNBC, as of 2025-07]; Tibet-local producers hold regional pricing power because hauling cement to Medog is prohibitive.

bottleneck.note: Regional quasi-monopoly (Xizang Tianlu named the major beneficiary); capacity vs 2030 schedule is the question.

impact.rationale: >16Mt of cement into a region where haul-in is prohibitive makes local capacity the direct bottleneck asset.

evidence.claim: Project implies >40M m3 concrete / >16Mt cement; Xizang Tianlu named the major beneficiary

crowdedness.rationale: Tianlu was the retail-favorite dam trade in China — the most crowded pure-play locally.

evidence.claim: Tianlu among the sharpest A-share movers on the announcement

capture.rationale: Regional quasi-monopoly at altitude: freight economics create genuine local pricing power.

evidence.claim: Tibet-local cement enjoys structural freight protection

repricing_check.note: A-share repricing was immediate; whether earnings estimates followed (leg 1) unverified — needs domestic consensus data the free stack lacks. Flag: possibly crowded AND repriced locally.

links.name: Hydro turbines & generators
links.role: Dongfang Electric holds ~45% of China's conventional hydro equipment market and could take ~54B yuan of orders from this project alone [CNBC, as of 2025-07]; Harbin Electric is the other domestic heavyweight.

bottleneck.note: 60 GW of high-head units is a decade of duopoly-scale work; A-shares repriced immediately — H-share discounts are the screen question.

impact.rationale: 60 GW of high-head units is roughly a decade of duopoly-scale work; largest single equipment pool in the project.

evidence.claim: Dongfang holds ~45% of China conventional hydro equipment; potential ~54B yuan from this project

crowdedness.rationale: The obvious equipment trade: A-shares jumped 10% on three consecutive days at announcement.

evidence.claim: Dongfang Electric Shanghai shares hit consecutive daily limits post-announcement

capture.rationale: Effective domestic duopoly (Dongfang/Harbin) with qualification lock-in and multi-decade service tails.

evidence.claim: Two domestic suppliers dominate large Chinese hydro units

repricing_check.note: Key open question: A-shares repriced on story, but 54B yuan lands over ~a decade — did estimates move proportionally? H-share (1072.HK) vs A-share spread is the screen entry point.

links.name: UHVDC transmission buildout
links.role: Moving ~60 GW from Medog to eastern load centers requires new ultra-high-voltage DC corridors: converter valves, transformers, and grid integration — the quieter industrial layer behind the turbine story.

bottleneck.note: UHVDC converter capability is concentrated in a handful of Chinese suppliers (NARI, XD Electric, TBEA); corridor siting and build time gates offtake.

impact.rationale: Moving ~60 GW east needs new UHVDC corridors; converter valves and transformers are a project-scale equipment pool on top of an already-tight grid cycle.

evidence.claim: Project power must reach eastern load centers via long-haul UHV transmission per plan coverage

crowdedness.rationale: A tier quieter than turbines: institutional China-grid names, thin retail narrative, near-zero Western attention.

evidence.claim: Transmission suppliers appear in specialist notes, not in mainstream beneficiary lists

capture.rationale: Converter-valve capability concentrated in NARI/XD/TBEA; genuine technology moat inside a regulated buyer market.

evidence.claim: UHVDC converter technology held by a handful of Chinese suppliers

links.name: Copper & conductors
links.role: Thousands of kilometers of HVDC lines plus 60 GW of machines add a marginal but global copper and aluminum-conductor demand leg — the most Western-investable raw-material angle.

bottleneck.note: Global commodity; this project moves sentiment more than balances — capture is the question, not availability.

impact.rationale: Real but marginal at global scale: one project's lines and machines shift copper demand sentiment more than balances.

evidence.claim: HVDC corridors plus 60 GW of machines add conductor demand across ~3,000 km distances

crowdedness.rationale: Nobody connects global copper names to this dam; the linkage is entirely unmapped.

evidence.claim: No copper name appears in any beneficiary coverage reviewed

capture.rationale: Global commodity economics; miners capture cycle, not project premia.

evidence.claim: Copper pricing is set by the global balance, not one buyer

links.name: Global hydro-equipment spillover
links.role: A decade of Chinese domestic hydro demand absorbs Chinese supplier capacity, tightening the global market Western utilities buy from (Andritz, Voith private, GE Vernova hydro) — the second-order link most accessible outside China.

bottleneck.note: Spillover thesis needs verification in Western hydro backlogs and pricing — a genuine run-heat question.

impact.rationale: China's domestic mega-demand absorbs Chinese supplier capacity exactly as the global hydro/pumped-storage cycle inflects — tightening the market Western utilities buy from.

evidence.claim: Andritz 2025 hydro order intake EUR 2.52B was a company record; Q1 2026 group intake a record EUR 3.6B, hydropower-led; H1 2026 backlog EUR 12.6B, +20.5% vs YE2025
IHA global pipeline >1,127 GW incl. 621 GW pumped storage

crowdedness.rationale: Essentially unmapped as a Medog consequence: Andritz-class names are covered as boring European industrials, not as beneficiaries of Chinese capacity absorption; zero retail narrative.

evidence.claim: No Western equipment name appears in dam beneficiary coverage; Andritz record orders covered only in trade/financial press

capture.rationale: Western hydro equipment is an Andritz/Voith/GE Vernova oligopoly with decades-long service annuities.

evidence.claim: Three suppliers dominate Western hydro equipment with aftermarket tails

links.name: India's counter-buildout (Siang UMP)
links.role: India accelerated the 11,000 MW Siang Upper Multipurpose Project (NHPC + NEEPCO, ~$10-13.2B, construction from ~2028) explicitly as a flood-buffer response to Medog [Wikipedia/EastMojo, as of 2026-03]; plus Assam flood-control works.

bottleneck.note: Land consent is the gating item (village MOUs signing through early 2026); Indian hydro EPC and NHPC are the direct exposure — T3 listings.

impact.rationale: An explicit $10-13.2B counter-program (Siang UMP, 11 GW) plus flood-control works, accelerating BECAUSE of Medog; construction from ~2028 fits the 2-5y window.

evidence.claim: Siang UMP (NHPC+NEEPCO) framed as flood-buffer response; village consent MOUs signing through early 2026

crowdedness.rationale: Indian retail knows NHPC as a PSU dividend stock, not as a Medog-response trade; Western attention nil.

evidence.claim: Siang coverage is regional-political, not investment-framed

capture.rationale: THE TRAP, Indian edition: PSU hydro earns regulated returns; EPC winners bid-competed. Volume without proportional capture.

evidence.claim: NHPC operates under regulated-return frameworks

links.name: Riparian risk & monitoring
links.role: Downstream flow risk for India/Bangladesh creates durable demand for satellite hydrology monitoring, early-warning systems, and eventually parametric flood covers — thin today, but the least-priced Western angle on the whole event.

bottleneck.note: Nascent; demand is real (India built new monitoring posts post-announcement) but revenue concentration per listed name is unproven — score honestly.

impact.rationale: Durable but slow-building demand: India added monitoring infrastructure post-announcement; parametric flood covers remain nascent.

evidence.claim: India expanded hydrological monitoring on the Siang/Brahmaputra after the announcement

crowdedness.rationale: The least-discussed link in the entire chain; no investment coverage connects EO/monitoring names to Brahmaputra risk.

evidence.claim: No monitoring or insurance name appears in any reviewed coverage

capture.rationale: Real capability moats (satellite EO) but revenue concentration per listed name is unproven for this use case.

evidence.claim: EO providers' hydrology revenue is a small slice of diversified books
